<!-- ============ MISSION ============ -->
<div class="mission">
  <div class="wrap mission-grid">
    <div>
      <h1>emissivity.org is the common reference point for laboratories and research groups working on the <strong>measurement, modelling, and engineering of the thermal radiative properties of materials</strong>.</h1>
      <p class="who">
        It maintains the research map of the field, indexes its open data resources,
        documents measurement standards and good practice, and keeps the community
        calendar. Editorially maintained by the community; hosted at the
        University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU).
      </p>
      <p class="quicklinks">
        <a href="/network/index.html">Research map</a> <span class="sep">·</span>
        <a href="/data/index.html">Data resources</a> <span class="sep">·</span>
        <a href="/methods/principles.html">What is emissivity?</a> <span class="sep">·</span>
        <a href="/events-news/conferences.html">Conference calendar</a>
      </p>
    </div>

<!-- ============ NETWORK ============ -->
<section class="home-section" id="network">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="sec-head">
      <h2>The research map</h2>
      <a class="more" href="/network/index.html">Full directory →</a>
    </div>
    <p class="sec-intro">
      A curated directory of the non-commercial institutions where emissivity and
      thermal radiative properties are actively researched — from national metrology
      institutes to planetary spectroscopy and engineered thermal emission.
      Inclusion criteria, tier logic, and limitations are documented in the
      <a href="/network/methodology.html">methodology</a>. Last revision: 2026-06.
    </p>

    <div class="net-stats" id="home-net-stats">
      <div class="net-stat"><div class="v" id="stat-inst">—</div><div class="k">institutions</div></div>
      <div class="net-stat"><div class="v" id="stat-countries">—</div><div class="k">countries</div></div>
      <div class="net-stat"><div class="v" id="stat-core">—</div><div class="k">core-tier laboratories</div></div>
      <div class="net-stat"><div class="v" id="stat-eco">—</div><div class="k">thematic ecosystems</div></div>
    </div>

    <div id="labmap" class="labmap" aria-label="World map of institutions on the research map"></div>
    <div class="map-legend">
      <span class="key"><span class="dot meas"></span> Measurement &amp; metrology laboratories</span>
      <span class="key"><span class="dot eng"></span> Engineered emissivity (thermal photonics, radiative cooling)</span>
      <span class="note">Each marker links to the institution's profile.</span>
    </div>

    <table class="dir">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Institution</th>

          <th>Tier</th>

        </tr>

      <tbody>

          <td><span class="tier-pill core">core</span></td>
          <td class="cap">Traceable spectral emissivity, −40 °C to ≈2300 °C, air and vacuum, near to far infrared.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="inst"><a href="/network/cemhti-cnrs.html">CEMHTI — CNRS</a>
            <span class="unit">High-temperature radiative properties, Orléans</span></td>
          <td class="cc">FR</td>
          <td><span class="tier-pill core">core</span></td>
          <td class="cap">Spectral emissivity of ceramics, glasses, and refractories above 1500 K.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="inst"><a href="/network/dlr-psl.html">DLR Institute of Planetary Research</a>
            <span class="unit">Planetary Spectroscopy Laboratory, Berlin</span></td>
          <td class="cc">DE</td>
          <td><span class="tier-pill core">core</span></td>
          <td class="cap">Vacuum FTIR emissivity 0.3 to &gt;100 µm, heated planetary-analog samples; Berlin Emissivity Database.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="inst"><a href="/network/thermomat-ehu.html">Thermomat / HAIRL — UPV/EHU</a>
            <span class="unit">Thermophysical properties group, Bilbao</span></td>
          <td class="cc">ES</td>
          <td><span class="tier-pill core">core</span></td>
          <td class="cap">FTIR directional spectral emissometry with uncertainty budget; maintainers of EKHI.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="inst"><a href="/network/promes-cnrs.html">PROMES — CNRS</a>
            <span class="unit">Solar furnace facilities, Odeillo</span></td>
          <td class="cc">FR</td>
          <td><span class="tier-pill core">core</span></td>
          <td class="cap">High-temperature radiative properties under concentrated solar flux; selective absorbers.</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="inst"><a href="/network/nist.html">National Institute of Standards and Technology</a>

<!-- ============ DATA RESOURCES ============ -->
<section class="home-section tinted" id="data">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="sec-head">
      <h2>Open data resources</h2>
      <a class="more" href="/data/index.html">All resources →</a>
    </div>
    <p class="sec-intro">
      The field's openly accessible databases of radiative and optical property data,
      each maintained by a member institution. Counts are exact and dated; every
      dataset is traceable to its source publication.
    </p>

    <div class="res">
      <div class="res-row">
        <div class="name"><a href="/data/ekhi.html">EKHI</a>
          <span class="by">Thermomat / UPV/EHU · Bilbao</span></div>
        <div class="desc">
          Open, publication-centred database of optical and thermal radiative properties
          of solid materials: curve-level spectral datasets with explicit provenance,
          machine-readable downloads, and citation tools. Described in
          <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-026-07083-9"><em>Scientific Data</em> (2026)</a>.
        </div>
        <div class="facts">
          1 251 curves · 167 publications<br/>
          0.05–1000 µm · counts at 2026-01<br/>
          <a href="https://thermomat.ehu.eus/ekhi">thermomat.ehu.eus/ekhi →</a>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="res-row">
        <div class="name"><a href="/network/dlr-psl.html">Berlin Emissivity Database</a>
          <span class="by">DLR Institute of Planetary Research</span></div>
        <div class="desc">
          Emissivity spectra of planetary-analog materials (minerals, regolith simulants)
          measured in vacuum, including heated samples for Mercury and Venus surface
          conditions. Supports the MERTIS instrument on BepiColombo.
        </div>
        <div class="facts">
          planetary analogs · vacuum FTIR<br/>
          <a href="/network/dlr-psl.html">maintainer profile →</a>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="res-row">
        <div class="name"><a href="https://speclib.jpl.nasa.gov">ECOSTRESS Spectral Library</a>
          <span class="by">NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory</span></div>
        <div class="desc">
          Laboratory reflectance and emissivity spectra of natural and man-made materials
          (formerly the ASTER Spectral Library), widely used for land-surface
          temperature and emissivity retrieval.
        </div>
        <div class="facts">
          natural + man-made materials<br/>
          <a href="https://speclib.jpl.nasa.gov">speclib.jpl.nasa.gov →</a>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="res-row">
        <div class="name"><a href="/network/usgs-spectroscopy.html">USGS Spectral Library</a>
          <span class="by">U.S. Geological Survey, Spectroscopy Lab</span></div>
        <div class="desc">
          Reference reflectance spectra of minerals, rocks, soils, vegetation, and
          man-made materials, used across remote sensing and as input for emissivity
          modelling.
        </div>
        <div class="facts">
          version 7 · open access<br/>
          <a href="/network/usgs-spectroscopy.html">maintainer profile →</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
